turns.input: *He asks Jessa Rook who they think he is and where he comes from.*
turns.draft:
Jessa Rook looks him over without hurry, the way she might size up a stranger at her own door — his hands, his clothes, his feet — before answering.

"Honestly? I don't know you," she says. "You don't have the look of the West District workshop men, and you're not dressed like a merchant I've served. If I had to guess from looking at you, I'd say you're new to Calderan — you've been standing in this square like a man waiting for someone to tell him where he is." She shrugs, unbothered. "As for where you come from, that's yours to tell or not. I only ask what I need to know."

She glances toward the tower's heavy entrance behind him, then back. "This square doesn't see many strangers with no luggage and no business. So — do you have business here, or are you just passing the time?"
